# Third-party code

## libvterm 0.3.3 (`deps/libvterm`, MIT, see its `LICENSE`)

The terminal state machine behind the `vterm` screen engine. Upstream lives in
Bazaar on Launchpad; this tree comes from the git mirror Neovim kept of it.

| What | Value |
|---|---|
| Added with | `git read-tree --prefix=deps/libvterm -u v0.3.3^{tree}` after fetching the tag: one plain commit, no merge, so history stays linear; its `git-subtree-dir:` / `git-subtree-split:` trailers are what `git subtree` reads |
| Upstream commit | `9d6d2112335080312ef8c36667fa717ded4f7daf` (tag `v0.3.3`) |
| Release tarball | `libvterm-0.3.3.tar.gz`, sha256 `09156f43dd2128bd347cbeebe50d9a571d32c64e0cf18d211197946aff7226e0`, the same file as Debian's `libvterm_0.3.3.orig.tar.gz` |
| Checked | `src/` and `include/` equal the tarball's, file for file |
| Tag vs tarball | The tag also has `doc/`, `CODE-MAP`, the `.tbl` sources and `tbl2inc_c.pl`; its `Makefile` and `vterm.pc.in` differ (the tarball strips the dist section); `t/69screen_sb_clear.test` is in the tarball only; the tarball has the generated `.inc` files (change 1) |

Changes on top of upstream, each its own commit (`git log -- deps/libvterm`):

1. `src/encoding/DECdrawing.inc` and `uk.inc`: generated by upstream's Makefile from the
   `.tbl` files with Perl; copied from the release tarball, which ships them, so a build
   needs only a C compiler.

2. `src/state.c`, REP (`CSI n b`, repeat the previous character): with no character drawn
   yet, `combine_width` is 0 and `while (pos.col < col) pos.col += combine_width` never
   ends, so one `ESC [ 3 b` as a terminal's first output froze the brain for good (no
   crash, so no restart). Now REP does nothing then, as ECMA-48 leaves it undefined.
   Found by tests/test_vterm.py on its second seed; libvterm's own screen layer hangs
   the same way. The same loop repeated a wide character into the last column, half
   past the row's end: libvterm's screen layer then writes through a NULL cell pointer
   (`screen.c` putglyph, a segfault; found on seed 46). Now a character is repeated
   only while it fits. Not reported upstream yet.

3. `src/state.c`, `on_resize`: only the bottom and right margins were clamped to the new
   size, so a scroll region that no longer fit (`ESC [ 6 ; 10 r`, then 3 rows) ended
   upside down, and the next line feed's `scroll()` did a `memmove` of negative size
   (found by AddressSanitizer on tests/test_vterm.py seed 10040; before it, a heap
   corruption). Such a region now goes back to the whole screen, as xterm resets
   margins on a resize. Not reported upstream yet.

4. `src/state.c`, `savecursor` (restore, `ESC 8`, leaving `?1049`): the saved position
   came back unclamped, so a cursor saved on row 4 and restored after a resize to 3 rows
   sat off the screen; the next glyph read and wrote `lineinfo` past its end, and
   libvterm's screen layer wrote through a NULL cell (AddressSanitizer, seed 103772
   of a 5000-seed run). Clamped to the screen now, as xterm restores a cursor. Not
   reported upstream yet.

5. `src/state.c`, `vterm_state_reset` (RIS, `ESC c`, what `reset` sends): it cleared
   the alternate-screen flag without telling the screen, so the screen (libvterm's, and
   py-screen's store) went on showing the alternate buffer while the state said primary.
   Found by tests/test_vterm.py once the scrollback was compared: after a RIS inside
   `?1049h`, a shrink pushed different rows in the two stores. RIS now leaves the
   alternate screen through the property, as `DECRST 1049` does. Not reported upstream yet.

6. `src/screen.c`, `resize_buffer`: the rows a shrink pushes to the scrollback were read
   with `vterm_screen_get_cell`, which reads the buffer shown, so with the alternate
   screen up it pushed the alternate screen's rows in place of the primary's. It now
   reads the buffer being resized. This is libvterm's own screen layer, which py-screen
   uses only as the test reference. Not reported upstream yet.

Nothing else in libvterm is changed; py-screen's own C code reaches libvterm through its
headers and, for its own resize, the line-info arrays and allocator libvterm's state
expects a resize callback to replace (as `screen.c` does).

To update, keep it flat the same way: fetch the new tag, `git rm -rq deps/libvterm`,
`git read-tree --prefix=deps/libvterm -u <tag>^{tree}`, commit with the two trailers
naming the new upstream commit, then redo change 1 from that release's tarball and
check its sha256 against Debian's `.dsc`. (`git subtree pull --squash` also works from
the trailers, tested 0.3.2 → 0.3.3, but it adds a merge commit.)
